designs.title: URL Shortener
designs.subtitle: Base62 IDs, a Read-Heavy Cache, 301 vs 302
designs.brief: Written as the reference chapter.

designs.title: Rate Limiter
designs.subtitle: Token Buckets and Sliding Windows in Redis
designs.brief: Distributed limiter at the API gateway: per-user / per-IP / per-key rules, rules service. Compare token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window, sliding log and sliding window counter (memory, burstiness, accuracy). Redis implementation with atomic Lua scripts (or INCR + EXPIRE) and the race it avoids; sharding counters by key with consistent hashing; multi-region (local limits plus async sync, or a global budget split per region); response contract (429, Retry-After, X-RateLimit-* headers); fail-open vs fail-closed when Redis is down; limiting at the client, edge and service.

designs.title: Distributed Key-Value Store
designs.subtitle: Dynamo-Style Partitioning, Replication and Quorums
designs.brief: get/put API at huge scale with tunable consistency. Consistent hashing with virtual nodes; replication factor N on the preference list; quorums R + W > N and what each setting buys; sloppy quorums and hinted handoff; conflict resolution with vector clocks vs last-write-wins; anti-entropy with Merkle trees; gossip membership and failure detection; storage engine as an LSM tree (commit log, memtable, SSTables, compaction as a k-way merge, Bloom filters to skip SSTables). Contrast with a leader-based design (Raft per shard).

designs.title: Distributed Cache
designs.subtitle: Cache-Aside, Eviction and Hot Keys
designs.brief: Memcached/Redis cluster in front of a database. Cache-aside vs read-through vs write-through vs write-back; eviction (LRU, LFU, TTL) and memory overhead; sharding with consistent hashing and what moves on resize; replication for availability; hot keys (local in-process cache, key replication / splitting); cache stampede (request coalescing, locks, probabilistic early expiration); keeping cache and DB consistent (delete-on-write and its race, versioned values, lease tokens as in Facebook's memcache paper); negative caching.

designs.title: News Feed (Twitter)
designs.subtitle: Fan-Out on Write, Fan-Out on Read, and the Celebrity Hybrid
designs.brief: Post, follow, home timeline, user timeline. Fan-out on write into per-user timeline caches (Redis lists of tweet ids, capped length) vs fan-out on read (merge followees' recent tweets, like Merge K Sorted Arrays) and the hybrid: push for normal accounts, pull for celebrities at read time. Tweet storage and IDs (Snowflake), social graph storage, media via object storage + CDN, ranking at a high level, cursor pagination, counters (likes/retweets) updated asynchronously, timeline cache warming for inactive users.

designs.title: Chat System (WhatsApp)
designs.subtitle: WebSocket Gateways, Receipts and the Offline Inbox
designs.brief: 1:1 and small-group chat with sent / delivered / read receipts. Persistent connections through WebSocket gateway servers; session registry (user -> gateway) in a fast store; send path (client -> gateway -> chat service -> recipient's gateway); per-conversation ordering with sequence numbers and client-side dedup by message id; offline delivery via an inbox store plus push notifications (APNs/FCM); group fan-out for small groups; message storage (wide-column, partitioned by conversation); media through object storage; end-to-end encryption at a high level (server stores ciphertext); reconnect and resync.

designs.title: Messenger
designs.subtitle: Multi-Device Sync, Presence and Search
designs.brief: Builds on Chapter 6 (refer to it rather than repeating). Multi-device: a per-user message log with a per-device cursor, so each device syncs by sequence number; read state across devices; presence (heartbeats, last-seen, fan-out of presence changes to friends with batching and throttling); typing indicators as ephemeral events; message history storage (HBase / Cassandra wide rows by user and time); message search with a per-user inverted index; large groups and channels.

designs.title: Video Platform (YouTube)
designs.subtitle: Chunked Upload, Transcoding and Adaptive Bitrate
designs.brief: Upload, process, watch. Resumable chunked upload to object storage (pre-signed URLs); transcoding pipeline as a DAG of tasks (split into segments, encode each segment to a bitrate ladder in parallel, package HLS/DASH, thumbnails), scheduled by a job system; metadata DB; delivery through a CDN; adaptive bitrate selection on the client; view counting at scale (approximate, aggregated); hot vs long-tail storage tiers. Recommendations out of scope.

designs.title: Streaming Service (Netflix)
designs.subtitle: Its Own CDN, Pre-Positioned Content and DRM
designs.brief: Control plane in the cloud (catalog, auth, recommendations, playback API) vs data plane on Netflix's own CDN appliances placed in ISPs (Open Connect). Proactive caching: predicted popularity pushes content to appliances during off-peak fill windows; steering a client to the best appliance; per-title encoding and adaptive bitrate; DRM license acquisition; playback start latency; resilience culture (chaos engineering) at a high level. Contrast with the YouTube chapter (Chapter 8).

designs.title: Cloud File Storage (Google Drive / Dropbox)
designs.subtitle: Chunking, Content-Hash Dedup and Sync Conflicts
designs.brief: Upload, download, sync across devices, share. Client splits files into chunks (fixed size, or content-defined with a rolling hash so an insertion only changes nearby chunks); content hash per chunk for dedup and integrity; upload only missing chunks; metadata DB (files, versions, chunk lists, namespaces) vs block storage; sync through a per-user change journal with cursors plus a notification channel (long poll / WebSocket); conflicts produce conflicted copies; sharing and ACLs; delta sync and compression.

designs.title: Collaborative Editor (Google Docs)
designs.subtitle: OT vs CRDT, Live Cursors and Revision History
designs.brief: Many users editing one document in real time. A document session pinned to one server (routing by doc id); operational transformation with a central server that orders operations by revision and transforms concurrent ones (show a small insert/insert transform); CRDT alternative (unique position ids) and when it wins (offline, peer-to-peer); presence and live cursors as ephemeral broadcasts; persistence as snapshots plus an operation log, revision history from it; offline edits and reconnect; comments and permissions briefly.

designs.title: Distributed Log (Kafka)
designs.subtitle: Partitions, Offsets, Consumer Groups and In-Sync Replicas
designs.brief: Topics split into partitions, each an append-only log of segment files with an offset index; producers choose partitions by key hash (ordering per key); acks = 0 / 1 / all; replication with leader and followers, in-sync replicas (ISR), high watermark; leader election via the controller (KRaft); consumer groups, partition assignment and rebalancing, committed offsets; delivery guarantees (at-most-once, at-least-once, exactly-once with idempotent producers and transactions); retention by time/size and log compaction; why sequential disk I/O and zero-copy make it fast.

designs.title: Ride Hailing (Uber)
designs.subtitle: Geospatial Index, Matching and Surge Pricing
designs.brief: Riders request, drivers stream locations (every few seconds). Location ingest into an in-memory geospatial index sharded by cell (geohash / quadtree / S2); nearby-driver search by expanding cell rings; matching and dispatch (offer to the best candidate, timeouts, re-offer); trip state machine; ETA from the road graph (Chapter 14); surge pricing per cell from supply/demand over sliding windows; payments handoff; consistency of driver state (one trip at a time).

designs.title: Maps and Navigation (Google Maps)
designs.subtitle: Road Graph, A*, Contraction Hierarchies, Tiles and Live ETA
designs.brief: Render maps and route. Map tiles as a zoom pyramid (vector tiles, CDN, tile coordinates); geocoding and search; routing on the road graph: Dijkstra -> A* with a straight-line heuristic -> contraction hierarchies (preprocessing shortcuts, bidirectional search) for continent-scale graphs; graph partitioning; live traffic from GPS probes updating edge weights; ETA prediction (historical + live); rerouting.

designs.title: Content Delivery Network
designs.subtitle: Edge PoPs, GeoDNS and Anycast, Cache Keys and Invalidation
designs.brief: Points of presence with tiered caches; routing users to a PoP (GeoDNS vs anycast BGP); within a PoP, consistent hashing of URLs to cache servers; cache keys, Vary and query-string normalization; TTLs, purge/invalidation and versioned URLs; origin shield to collapse misses; pull vs push CDN; TLS termination at the edge; hot content and request coalescing; failure of a PoP.

designs.title: Search Autocomplete
designs.subtitle: Top-K per Prefix, Log Aggregation and Caching
designs.brief: Suggest the top 5-10 queries for each typed prefix within ~100 ms. Data pipeline: query logs aggregated (batch daily + streaming for trending) into counts; build a trie with the top-k completions cached at every node; serve from memory, sharded by prefix range, replicated; browser and CDN caching of popular prefixes; update by rebuilding and swapping snapshots; filtering offensive terms; typo tolerance and personalization only as extensions.

designs.title: Web Crawler
designs.subtitle: URL Frontier, Politeness, Dedup and Recrawl
designs.brief: Crawl billions of pages. Seed URLs -> URL frontier with priority queues and per-host back queues (Mercator design) for politeness; robots.txt and crawl-delay; DNS caching; fetchers and parsers; URL normalization and dedup with a Bloom filter (or a sharded seen-set); content dedup with simhash/fingerprints; storing pages (object store / Bigtable); recrawl scheduling by change rate; crawler traps; distributing the frontier by host hash.

designs.title: Discussion Forum (Reddit)
designs.subtitle: Nested Comments, Votes and Hot Ranking
designs.brief: Communities, posts, nested comments, votes. Comment tree storage (adjacency list with parent_id plus a path/depth, loading top N children by score and expanding lazily); vote storage (one vote per user per item, idempotent) and score counters updated asynchronously; ranking algorithms: hot (log of score plus time decay), best (Wilson score lower bound), top, new; caching ranked listings per community; precomputing front pages; moderation basics.

designs.title: Photo Sharing (Instagram)
designs.subtitle: Photo Storage, Feed and Stories
designs.brief: Upload photos, follow, feed, stories. Upload pipeline (pre-signed upload to object storage, resize into several resolutions, CDN); metadata DB; feed generation reusing the fan-out ideas of Chapter 5 with ranking; stories with a 24-hour expiry (TTL), per-viewer tray of followees with fresh stories, seen state; likes and comments counters; explore at a high level.

designs.title: Notification System
designs.subtitle: Push, SMS and Email with Retries and Idempotency
designs.brief: Services ask to notify users through push (APNs/FCM), SMS and email. Notification service API, user preferences and opt-outs, templates and localization; per-channel queues and workers calling providers; retries with exponential backoff and jitter, dead-letter queues; idempotency keys to avoid duplicates; rate limiting per user and per provider; scheduled and batched notifications (digests); delivery tracking and analytics; provider failover.

designs.title: Unique ID Generator
designs.subtitle: Snowflake, Ticket Servers and UUIDs
designs.brief: Generate unique 64-bit, roughly time-sortable ids at high throughput without coordination. Options compared: UUIDv4 (128 random bits), UUIDv7 (time-ordered), a database auto-increment (single point), ticket servers with offsets/steps (Flickr), range/block allocation, and Snowflake (41-bit time, 10-bit machine, 12-bit sequence). Machine id assignment (ZooKeeper / config), clock skew and NTP, behaviour when the clock moves backwards, sequence overflow, ids as cursors.

designs.title: Web Search Engine
designs.subtitle: Inverted Index, Sharding and Ranking
designs.brief: From crawled pages (Chapter 17) to ranked results. Indexing pipeline: parse, tokenize, build postings lists (doc ids, term frequency, positions) and compress them; partition the index by document (scatter-gather to all shards, merge top-k) vs by term; query processing (intersect postings, phrase queries with positions, early termination); ranking: BM25/TF-IDF, PageRank, learning to rank in stages; result caching; index freshness tiers (realtime vs base index); replicas for QPS.

designs.title: Top-K Trending Topics
designs.subtitle: Count-Min Sketch and Windowed Aggregation
designs.brief: Top hashtags/videos in the last minute, hour, day. Event stream (Kafka) -> stream processor with tumbling/sliding windows; exact counts per partition plus a top-k heap, merging partial top-k lists from partitions (and why that can miss items); approximate heavy hitters with count-min sketch + heap (or space-saving); trending as a rate of change against a baseline; batch layer for exact daily results (lambda) vs streaming only (kappa); serving precomputed results.

designs.title: Payment System
designs.subtitle: Idempotency Keys, Double-Entry Ledger and Reconciliation
designs.brief: Accept payments through a payment service provider (PSP). Payment state machine; idempotency keys on every API and on calls to the PSP; double-entry ledger (immutable entries, balances derived from them); asynchronous PSP results via webhooks; retries and timeouts without double charging; reconciliation against PSP settlement files; transactional outbox and sagas for cross-service consistency; exactly-once effects; security (PCI scope via tokenization).

designs.title: Ticket Booking (Ticketmaster)
designs.subtitle: Seat Holds with a TTL, a Waiting Room and No Overselling
designs.brief: Browse events, view seat map, hold seats, pay, confirm. Seat holds with a TTL (Redis SET NX PX, or a DB row with expires_at) so abandoned carts release seats; confirming with a conditional update (no overselling); payment integration; a virtual waiting room for hot on-sales (admission tokens, queue position, rate of admission); search through a search index; caching seat maps; bots and fairness.

designs.title: Hotel Booking (Airbnb)
designs.subtitle: Availability Calendars and No Double Bookings
designs.brief: Search by place and dates, view, book. Geo + date availability search (index of listings plus availability calendars); inventory as rows per room type per date (or per listing per night) with constraints; booking flow with concurrency control: pessimistic locks vs optimistic versioning vs database constraints, and why a unique constraint per (listing, night) is the simplest guarantee; idempotent reservations; holds during payment; overbooking policy for hotels; cancellations.

designs.title: Proximity Search (Yelp)
designs.subtitle: Geohash, Quadtrees and Nearby Places
designs.brief: Find businesses near a point within a radius, ranked. Business data changes rarely, reads dominate. Options: lat/long range queries with indexes, geohash prefixes plus the 8 neighbouring cells, an in-memory quadtree rebuilt periodically, S2/H3 cells; precision vs radius; ranking by distance and rating; read replicas and caching; reviews and photos as separate services; scaling the index by region.

designs.title: Ad Click Aggregator
designs.subtitle: Exactly-Once Stream Counting
designs.brief: Count ad clicks per ad per minute for billing and dashboards. Click redirect service logs events; dedup (click id, Bloom filter / keyed state); Kafka; stream aggregation (Flink) with event-time windows, watermarks and late events; exactly-once via checkpoints and idempotent/transactional sinks; OLAP store for queries; periodic batch reconciliation against raw logs; hot ads (key splitting); fraud filtering.

designs.title: Metrics and Monitoring
designs.subtitle: Time-Series Storage, Downsampling and Alerting
designs.brief: Collect metrics from 100k hosts, query dashboards, alert. Pull (Prometheus) vs push collection; ingestion via Kafka; time-series database: series = metric name + labels, chunked storage with delta-of-delta timestamps and XOR-compressed values (Gorilla); label index; retention and downsampling rollups; query engine; alert rules evaluated on a schedule, deduplicated and routed; cardinality explosion and how to cap it; percentiles via sketches.

designs.title: Distributed Job Scheduler
designs.subtitle: Leader Election and At-Least-Once Execution
designs.brief: Run cron-like and one-off jobs reliably across a cluster. Job definitions in a DB; scheduler (leader elected via a lease in ZooKeeper/etcd) scans due jobs in time buckets and enqueues executions; workers pull from the queue with visibility timeouts and heartbeats; at-least-once execution with idempotent jobs; retries with backoff; job dependencies as a DAG (topological order); partitioning the scheduler by job id for scale; missed-run policies; observability.

designs.title: Leaderboard
designs.subtitle: Sorted Sets and Sharded Ranks
designs.brief: Update a player's score, top N, a player's rank and neighbours. Redis sorted set (skip list) for one leaderboard and its complexity; persistence and rebuilding from the source of truth; scaling to hundreds of millions of players: shard by score range, or approximate rank via score histograms / counting buckets (segment tree over score buckets); ties; periodic leaderboards (daily/weekly) with keys per period; friends leaderboards.

designs.title: Live Streaming and Live Comments (Twitch)
designs.subtitle: Low-Latency Ingest and Real-Time Fan-Out
designs.brief: Broadcasters stream live video; viewers watch with low latency and chat. Ingest (RTMP/SRT) to the nearest ingest PoP; real-time transcoding into a bitrate ladder; packaging into low-latency HLS segments and CDN fan-out; the latency budget end to end; live comments via a pub/sub layer and WebSocket/SSE fan-out servers subscribed per stream; sharding hot streams; chat rate limits and moderation; VOD recording.

designs.title: Object Storage (S3)
designs.subtitle: Metadata Service, Erasure Coding and Durability
designs.brief: PUT/GET/DELETE/LIST objects in buckets at exabyte scale. Separation of a partitioned metadata service (key -> placement, versions) from data nodes; write path; replication vs erasure coding (e.g. Reed-Solomon 6+3 or 10+4) and the durability/overhead trade; durability math intuition; multipart upload; strong read-after-write consistency; LIST with prefix and delimiter (sorted key index); garbage collection and repair of lost fragments; storage classes.

designs.title: E-Commerce Checkout and Inventory
designs.subtitle: Reservations and Flash Sales
designs.brief: Cart, checkout, payment, order. Inventory reservation with a TTL during checkout; order state machine; payment via Chapter 24; preventing oversell (atomic decrement in Redis plus DB as source of truth, or conditional updates); flash sales: pre-loading inventory tokens, queueing buyers, rate limiting and bot protection; idempotent order creation; eventual consistency of inventory across warehouses.

designs.title: Music Streaming (Spotify)
designs.subtitle: Catalog, Playback and Offline Downloads
designs.brief: Catalog metadata service; audio files encoded at several bitrates in object storage, delivered by CDN with prefetch of the next track; playlists (collaborative); offline downloads with DRM and license checks; play events for royalties and analytics (exactly-counted per stream); search over the catalog; recommendations at a high level (Chapter 47).

designs.title: Video Conferencing (Zoom)
designs.subtitle: WebRTC, SFU vs MCU
designs.brief: Real-time audio/video for 2-1000 participants. Signaling service; NAT traversal with ICE/STUN/TURN; media over UDP (SRTP); topologies: mesh vs SFU (forward streams, simulcast/SVC layers per receiver) vs MCU (mix and re-encode) and their CPU/bandwidth trade-offs; bandwidth estimation and adaptation; jitter buffers; cascading SFUs across regions for large meetings; recording; meeting placement on servers.

designs.title: Distributed File System (GFS / HDFS)
designs.subtitle: A Master, Chunkservers and Replication
designs.brief: Store huge files for batch processing. Files split into large chunks (64-128 MB); a master holds the namespace and chunk locations in memory with an operation log and checkpoints; chunkservers store replicas (usually 3) with rack awareness; reads go to the master for locations, then directly to chunkservers; writes with leases and a primary that orders mutations, pipelined data flow; record append; re-replication and balancing; master high availability (shadow masters / HDFS NameNode HA) and federation.

designs.title: Globally Distributed Database (Spanner)
designs.subtitle: Paxos Groups and TrueTime
designs.brief: SQL with external consistency across continents. Data split into ranges (splits/tablets), each replicated by a Paxos group across zones with a leader; TrueTime returns an interval [earliest, latest] and commit wait makes timestamps match real time order; read-write transactions with two-phase locking and two-phase commit across Paxos groups; lock-free snapshot reads at a timestamp; read-only transactions; placement and directories; the cost of commit wait and why GPS/atomic clocks keep it small.

designs.title: Coordination Service (Chubby / ZooKeeper)
designs.subtitle: Consensus, Sessions and Leases
designs.brief: Small, highly available metadata and locks. Replicated state machine on 5 servers via consensus (Paxos / ZAB / Raft): leader, log, quorum commits; a filesystem-like namespace (znodes); sessions with heartbeats and ephemeral nodes; watches; sequential nodes for distributed locks and leader election (without the herd effect); fencing tokens against stale leaders; read scaling with followers and its consistency caveat; typical uses (service discovery, config, leader election).

designs.title: Load Balancer and API Gateway
designs.subtitle: L4 vs L7, Health Checks and Routing
designs.brief: Spread traffic over servers and expose one front door. L4 (connection level, ECMP, consistent hashing as in Maglev) vs L7 (HTTP routing, TLS termination); algorithms: round robin, weighted, least connections, power of two choices, consistent hashing for stickiness; health checks and connection draining; high availability of the balancer itself (active-passive with VRRP, anycast); API gateway duties: authentication, rate limiting, request routing and transformation, retries and circuit breaking, observability.

designs.title: Pastebin
designs.subtitle: Text Blobs, Short Keys and Expiry
designs.brief: Paste text, get a short link, read it, expire it. Compare with Chapter 1: payloads are kilobytes to megabytes, so content goes to object storage and metadata to a database; key generation via a pre-generated key service or counters + base62; expiry cleanup (TTL index or periodic sweeper); CDN caching of popular pastes; size limits and abuse controls; private/unlisted pastes.

designs.title: Email Service (Gmail)
designs.subtitle: SMTP, Mailbox Storage, Search and Spam
designs.brief: Send, receive, store, search mail for a billion users. Inbound SMTP (MX) servers; spam and malware filtering pipeline; mailbox storage partitioned by user (messages, labels as tags, threads); outbound queue with retries and backoff, DKIM/SPF signing; attachments in object storage (dedup by hash); per-user inverted index for search; client sync (IMAP/push, change history ids); quotas.

designs.title: Stock Exchange Matching Engine
designs.subtitle: Order Books and Price-Time Priority
designs.brief: Accept orders and match them fairly with microsecond latency. Order gateway with risk checks; a sequencer that gives every order a total order; matching engine per symbol in memory: order book of price levels each with a FIFO queue (best bid/ask via sorted maps or heaps), limit and market orders, partial fills; trade reports and market data fan-out; deterministic replay from the sequenced log for primary/backup failover; single-threaded design for determinism; latency techniques at a high level.

designs.title: Digital Wallet
designs.subtitle: Balances, Transfers and Event Sourcing
designs.brief: Hold balances and move money between users with correctness. Double-entry ledger; transfers within a shard (single transaction) vs across shards (two-phase commit, or sagas / TC-C with compensations); event sourcing: commands -> validated events in an append-only log -> state derived and snapshotted; idempotency; reconciliation; scaling by partitioning accounts; reproducibility and audit.

designs.title: Calendar (Google Calendar)
designs.subtitle: Events, Recurrence and Free/Busy
designs.brief: Create events, invite, see free/busy, get reminders. Event model with recurrence rules (RRULE) stored as rule plus exceptions, expanded for a window on read; time zones and daylight saving; invitations and RSVPs (per-attendee copies vs shared event); free/busy queries by merging attendees' busy intervals; reminders through a scheduler; sharing ACLs; sync with clients (sync tokens).

designs.title: Online Judge (LeetCode)
designs.subtitle: Sandboxed Execution and Queued Submissions
designs.brief: Users submit code; the system compiles and runs it against tests and returns a verdict. Problem and test-case storage; submission queue; worker fleet running code in sandboxes (containers, gVisor/Firecracker, seccomp, time and memory limits, no network); result storage and polling/WebSocket updates; contests: spikes, autoscaling, fairness, live leaderboard (Chapter 31); plagiarism and abuse prevention.

designs.title: Recommendation System
designs.subtitle: Candidate Generation, Ranking and Feedback
designs.brief: Recommend items (videos/products) to users. Two-stage funnel: candidate generation (collaborative filtering, embeddings with approximate nearest neighbour search, popular/fresh sources) then a ranking model over features from a feature store, then re-ranking for diversity and business rules; offline training vs online serving; logging impressions and feedback; A/B testing; cold start; latency budget per stage.

designs.title: Distributed Logging
designs.subtitle: Collect, Ship, Index and Retain
designs.brief: Centralize logs from thousands of services. Agents tail files and ship with buffering and backpressure; Kafka as the buffer; processors parse, enrich and route; an indexing store (inverted index, e.g. Elasticsearch) for recent logs and cheap object storage for the archive; structured logs and trace ids for correlation; sampling and rate limits for noisy services; retention tiers; querying and alerting on logs.

designs.title: Feature Flag and Config Service
designs.subtitle: Targeting Rules, Gradual Rollouts and Fast Propagation
designs.brief: Turn features on for some users without deploys. Flag definitions with targeting rules; percentage rollouts by hashing (flag, user id) into buckets so a user's assignment is stable; evaluation inside SDKs from a locally cached rule set; propagation via streaming (SSE) or polling with versions; defaults and fail-safe behaviour when the service is down; audit log, kill switches, stale flag cleanup; experiments integration.

designs.title: Like and View Counter at Scale
designs.subtitle: Sharded Counters and Approximate Counts
designs.brief: Count likes and views for billions of items with hot spikes. Likes are idempotent per (user, item): store the relationship, derive the count; views are high-volume increments: buffer in memory and flush, sharded sub-counters to avoid a hot row, stream aggregation via Kafka; eventual consistency for display vs exactness for billing; approximate unique viewers (HyperLogLog); hot items; reconciling counts.
